summary: This is the Argo Workflows documentation page on conditionals, which show how to run workflow steps only when a condition holds. Conditional execution uses the govaluate expression library, which supports complex syntax. The page gives a coin-flip example with a steps template, including compound and regex conditions, and a note on handling parameter values that contain quotes by using an expr expression instead.
one_line: Argo Workflows documentation on conditional step execution using govaluate-based `when` expressions, including a coin-flip example and nested-quote handling.
key_facts: Argo Workflows supports conditional execution of steps using a syntax implemented by govaluate.
The govaluate library is referenced from the Argo conditionals page as offering support for complex syntax.
The coin-flip example's flip-coin step is a script using image python:alpine3.6 that prints either "heads" or "tails" based on random.randint(0,1).
The heads step runs when the condition "{{steps.flip-coin.outputs.result}} == heads" is true.
The tails step runs when the condition "{{steps.flip-coin.outputs.result}} == tails" is true.
The complex-condition step calls the heads-tails-or-twice-tails template when the first flip was heads and the second was tails, or both were tails.
The heads-regex step uses the condition "{{steps.flip-again.outputs.result}} =~ hea" to match a regex.
The tails-regex step uses the condition "{{steps.flip-again.outputs.result}} =~ tai" to match a regex.
The heads and tails templates use image alpine:3.6 and echo "it was heads" or "it was tails".
If a parameter value contains quotes, it may invalidate the govaluate expression.
To handle parameters with quotes, the page recommends embedding an expr expression in the conditional.
The page is part of the Argo Workflows User Guide walk-through section and is documented in the Argo Workflows docs site built with Material for MkDocs.
